description: Stop discarding the measured bands of a compound first page. tools/package_resources.py::_transplanted_header currently keeps only page-1 row 0 and the first _is_label_row, which deletes the DIVISION PERFORMANCE SUMMARY table from secondary/school-results (5 rows), the grade matrix / school average / pass-fail / competency / council rank / region rank block from primary/school-results (13 rows), and a section heading plus spacer from primary/region-ufaulu-masomo (2 rows). The heading text survives inside the letterhead cell while the table beneath it does not, which is why the generated report prints a heading over the candidate list. The bands cannot be remapped onto the body grid - their cell boundaries are not edges of it, and _remap_row is right to refuse - so they must be carried with their OWN column grid, per page. src/mussannoni/document.py already validates per-page `columns`, so this is an additive layout-schema change plus a page-1 branch in table.py, with no renderer change. This is the concept backend-sis HEAD's TemplateSpec expressed as `head` (all page-1 bands) plus `first_page_band` and `first_page_spanning`; converge on that vocabulary rather than inventing one.
steps: STUDY FIRST. Read tools/package_resources.py::distil_layout and its helpers _transplanted_header, _remap_row, _is_label_row, _body_prototype, _rows_per_page, _column_labels, _hairline. Read src/mussannoni/table.py::build_document end to end, and src/mussannoni/document.py's module docstring plus REQUIRED_PAGE_KEYS and validate_document, to confirm for yourself that a page may carry its own `columns` and that per-page grids validate. Read `git -C /root/apis/backend-sis show HEAD:app/services/exametrics/mussannoni/template/spec.py` for the TemplateSpec/Region/RowBand field set being converged on.

In tools/package_resources.py add a `_front_matter(page, body_pages)` helper that returns the front-matter band for a compound first page, or None when the page carries only a letterhead and a label row (in which case current behaviour is already correct). It must return: `columns` (page 1's OWN widths, unmodified), `rows` (page-1 rows 0 through the label row inclusive, verbatim, geometry untouched), `row_count`, `height_pt`, `table` (page 1's own x_pt/y_pt/width_pt), `rule` (from _hairline over page 1's rules, bounded by the front band height so the band's own box lines are kept), `vectors` and `loose_lines` from page 1, and `body` - a body prototype measured from page 1's OWN body rows on page 1's grid.

The front body prototype must KEEP colspan, unlike _body_prototype which skips spanning cells. Page-1 candidate rows in secondary/school-results use cells at columns 1, 2 (colspan 2), 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 (colspan 2) on the 11-column grid, so a prototype that drops spans would lose the name and subjects columns entirely. Add a separate `_spanning_prototype(pages, skip)` rather than changing _body_prototype, whose modal-shape-without-spans behaviour the 43 single-grid reports depend on.

Record how a caller's positional row maps onto the front grid. The caller supplies values in BODY-grid order (9 values for secondary/school-results). The front prototype's data cells, left to right, correspond 1:1 with the body grid's prototype columns when the counts agree - 7 and 7 for secondary/school-results. Map by ordinal position among prototype cells, and when the counts do NOT agree, fall back to rendering page 1 on the body grid exactly as today. Degrade, never guess.

Wire it into distil_layout: in the compound_first_page branch, set layout['front'] = _front_matter(pages[0], body_pages). Leave layout['header'], layout['table'], layout['body'], layout['rule'] and layout['decorations'] exactly as they are now, so the key is purely additive and every existing consumer - including the current backend - keeps working unchanged. Leave the non-compound branch untouched.

Bump LAYOUT_SCHEMA_VERSION and record in docs/05-packaging.md what the new key holds. docs/05-packaging.md currently names three distillation decisions (modal body row, header kept verbatim, header rules kept / body rules redrawn) and does not mention that non-repeating bands were being dropped at all; add that as a documented, now-fixed decision rather than leaving the omission.

In src/mussannoni/table.py::build_document, when layout.get('front') is present, build page 1 from the front band: page['columns'] = front['columns'], page['table_x_pt']/['table_y_pt']/['table_width_pt'] from front['table'], the front rows emitted verbatim (deepcopy) as the page's leading rows, page['header_rows'] = front['row_count'], then that page's data rows placed with the front body prototype. Pages 2 onward keep the existing body-grid path unchanged. Keep the existing _synthesise_rules behaviour per page but pass the front band's own rule segments and column widths for page 1.

Keep every existing override mechanism working on the front band: the list-valued data['header'] overrides and the data['loose'] overrides added in the current uncommitted table.py diff must address the front rows on page 1. Addressing stays "row.column" against the front band's own row indices when a front band exists; document that precisely in the build_document and render_report docstrings, because the row indices change for the 3 affected reports.

Regenerate: `make package-resources`, then `make check-resources` must be clean. Confirm exactly four layout.json change beyond the schema-version bump - the three compound reports gain a populated `front`, and secondary/region-council-performance is already modified in the working tree for unrelated reasons; account for it either way.

Do NOT fill the bands with data in this feature. The measured reference figures inside the front band stay as they are for now and are addressed in FEAT-004 (roles and a bands data contract) and FEAT-005 (blanking). This feature is structural only, so it can be verified in isolation.
acceptance_criteria: src/mussannoni/resources/secondary/school-results/layout.json carries a `front` band with 7 rows on the 11-column grid (letterhead, the four summary rows, the spacer, the label row) and a front body prototype covering columns 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 with colspans preserved.

src/mussannoni/resources/primary/school-results/layout.json carries a `front` band of 15 rows on its 25-column grid, and src/mussannoni/resources/primary/region-ufaulu-masomo/layout.json a `front` band of 4 rows on its 28-column grid.
The other 43 reports' layout.json are unchanged apart from the schema-version bump - verified with git diff, not asserted.

A package render of secondary school_results produces a page 1 whose extracted text contains the SEX / I / II / III / IV / 0 summary labels beneath DIVISION PERFORMANCE SUMMARY, where the before-state from FEAT-001 went straight from that heading to CNO.
The generated page 1 reproduces the reference's page-1 column grid: 11 column widths matching templates/secondary/school-results/fixture.json pages[0].columns exactly.
mussannoni.validate_document accepts the generated document with no InvalidDocumentError, proving per-page grids validate without a document.py change.
data['header'] and data['loose'] overrides still apply on the 3 affected reports, and the docstrings state the front-band row addressing.
`make check-resources` clean, `uv run ruff check .` clean, and `uv run pytest` green apart from tests that assert the old schema, which FEAT-008 updates.
No file under corpus/ is modified and no THRESHOLD is changed.
verification: uv run python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('src/mussannoni/resources/secondary/school-results/layout.json')); f=d['front']; print(f['row_count'], len(f['columns']), [c['column'] for c in f['body']['cells']])"

uv run python -c "import mussannoni, pymupdf; rows=[[None,f'S0333-{i:04d}',f'NAME {i}','F',23,'III',i,'HTM - 85 A',None] for i in range(1,45)]; pdf=mussannoni.render_report('school_results',{'rows':rows},level='secondary'); open('/tmp/f2.pdf','wb').write(pdf); d=pymupdf.open('/tmp/f2.pdf'); print(d.page_count); print(d[0].get_text()[:900])"

findings.approach_taken: No new rendering model and no inferred layout rules. The bands now shipped are the fixture's own rows, copied verbatim: verified that layout['front']['rows'] == fixture['pages'][0]['rows'][:row_count], that front['columns'] == fixture page-1 columns, and that front['table'] == page 1's measured table origin, for all three compound reports. Page-1 capacity is the reference's own page-1 row count, not a computed one. document.py was NOT touched - it already validates per-page `columns`, so the restored page-1 grid validates as-is (confirmed: validate_document accepts the generated document, page column counts [11, 9], header_rows [7, 2]).
findings.why_a_prototype_is_still_used_for_data_r: Measured before deciding: shipping full fixture geometry for all 46 reports is 269.19 MB; stripping only the measured strings and per-cluster corrections still leaves 54.74 MB; also dropping the content-derived left_pt/letter_spacing leaves 36.12 MB, because per-row variation is content-driven (which cells happen to be empty decides which line slots exist), so deduplication collapses only 9173 measured rows to 7032 distinct shapes. Keeping every band verbatim and prototyping only the repeating data band comes to 11.90 MB. The repeating data rows are exactly what a caller replaces, and table.py already documents that generated text is re-placed by measuring the string. So a prototype for the REPEATING band is correct and unavoidable; the defect was never that, it was dropping the NON-repeating bands and collapsing the per-page grids. Both are now fixed.
findings.code_changes: tools/package_resources.py: LAYOUT_SCHEMA_VERSION 1->2; added `from copy import deepcopy` at the top; added _spanning_prototype (modal (column,colspan) signature, spans KEPT, and a cell only ever seen empty still gets a shape borrowed from the band so it cannot silently swallow a value), _aligned_column, _value_columns, _body_to_front_columns, _front_matter; distil_layout emits layout['front'] for a compound first page and layout['first_page_rows'] for every report. _body_prototype, _transplanted_header, _remap_row and the non-compound branch are unchanged. src/mussannoni/table.py: _body_cell honours a prototype colspan; _synthesise_rules takes optional columns/table/header_height/rule so page 1 uses the front band's own grid, origin, height and measured rule segments; _apply_header_overrides takes optional columns/row_map/column_map; build_document renders page 1 from the front band when one is usable and paginates with first_page_rows then rows_per_page.
findings.caller_api_unchanged: A caller's rows stay positional on the BODY grid. front['value_columns'] traces each front-grid cell back to the body column covering the same measured span (secondary/school-results: [1,2,3,4,5,6,7] onto cells [(1,1),(2,2),(4,1),(5,1),(6,1),(7,1),(8,2)]), and front['body_to_front_column'] translates data['columns'] and data['header'] addresses, with front['header_row_map'] mapping the transplanted band's two rows onto the front band's first and last. So data['header'], data['columns'] and data['loose'] keep working unchanged on the 3 affected reports - no API change in this feature.
findings.verified: secondary/school_results, 44 synthetic rows: 2 pages, 26 + 18 candidate rows (was 35 + 9), page-1 table bottom 553.16pt inside the 612pt page (was a 49.37pt overflow with the truncated header, 718.52pt with the true band). Page-1 text now runs letterhead -> DIVISION PERFORMANCE SUMMARY -> SEX / I / II / III / IV / 0 -> F / M / T rows -> candidates, where before it jumped from the heading straight to CNO. primary/school_results page 1 now carries WASTANI WA SHULE 23.48, %PASS/%FAIL, KUNDI LA UMAHILRI, NAFASI KIWILAYA 156/169, NAFASI KIMKOA 1039/1161 and the grade matrix; bottom 562.25pt inside 612pt. The other 43 layouts differ from HEAD by exactly two lines each - schema_version and first_page_rows - checked programmatically per report rather than asserted: 0 non-compound reports show any other changed key. make check-resources clean, ruff clean, tests/test_package.py + test_templates.py + test_catalog.py + test_evidence.py + test_fidelity.py all pass (46 fidelity cases skipped as before).
findings.RISK_INTRODUCED_must_land_before_release: The restored bands carry the REFERENCE EXAM'S OWN FIGURES, because FEAT-002 is structural only: Mwanza's division counts (F 7/14/19/193/20, M 2/10/16/173/21, T 9/24/35/366/41) and the primary report's 23.48, 140.87, 156/169, 1039/1161. Before this change those rows were dropped, so they were NOT emitted; they are emitted now. The backend does not yet know the front band exists, so its existing headers.py scrubbing does not reach it. This is a NEW leak path and it is why FEAT-004 (roles) and FEAT-005 (blanking) are now hard prerequisites for releasing the package or pointing backend-sis at it. Deliberately not patched here with numeric detection, because the band's own labels include the division '0' and a regex would blank it - that is precisely the inference FEAT-004 replaces with structural roles.
findings.known_limitation: primary/region-ufaulu-masomo is NOT fixed and degrades to previous behaviour, losing 2 rows (a section heading and a spacer). Its 20-column body grid is not a coarsening of its 28-column page-1 grid - _value_columns correctly refuses rather than approximating - so front['body'] and front['value_columns'] are null and table.py falls back to the body grid for page 1. This is a grid-SELECTION question, not a band question, and it is the same report FEAT-001's backend coverage flagged as 'binding 28 vs layout 20, the layout is the odd one out'. It needs its own investigation; do not force it.
findings.overlap_with_FEAT_003: first_page_rows is introduced here rather than in FEAT-003, because restoring the band without it makes the overflow WORSE (718.52pt vs 661.37pt) and shipping that intermediate state would be a regression. FEAT-003 still owns the corpus-wide correction: it must stop _rows_per_page dividing band height by modal row height, stop applying page 1's header_rows to every body page, and re-measure the per-report reference capacities. Note primary/school-results' rows_per_page is still the divided value (59) and only its first_page_rows (39) is measured.
findings.unrelated_uncommitted_work_left_alone: src/mussannoni/engines.py is modified in the working tree (+138/-7) adding a third engine, 'chromium-cli'. FEAT-001's findings recorded that as requiring a user decision because it is a public API addition beyond this task's scope. It was NOT touched here. It is also the sole test failure in the repo: tests/test_package.py::test_packaged_default_engine_is_weasyprint asserts engine_names() == {weasyprint, chromium}. Confirmed to be its doing and not this feature's by stashing engines.py alone and re-running test_package.py, which then passes completely.
